newsitem.title: UK: Pilot indpendent directors say to resign.
newsitem.headline: Pilot indpendent directors say to resign.

text.p: Pilot Investment Trust plc's independent directors said on Thursday they would resign following the acquisition of a controlling stake in Pilot by Undervalued Assets Trust plc.
In a statement, they said they had met a representative of UAT and its proposed new investment manager for Pilot, Scottish Value Management Ltd (SVM), on Wednesday.
UAT requested that the directors recommend UAT's offers for Pilot shares and warrants, and replace the existing investment manager Rutherford Asset Management with SVM.

They said they were not prepared to replace Rutherford as shareholders should not have to bear the cost of two investment managers until Rutherford's management agreement expired. Also they believed Rutherford would manage the portfolio competently.

But as UAT had the power to replace the directors by people nominated by UAT and the independent directors, they said they would convene a board meeting at which they would appoint directors independent of SVM, and then resign.

The directors said they were recommending share and warrant holders consider selling their Pilot shares in the market or accepting UAT's offers as they saw no advantage to those who have not accepted the offer remaining a shareholder in Pilot.
They said they expected a special dividend proposed by UAT will be declared at the board meeting.
UAT said on Monday it had won control of Pilot with a 51.6 percent stake, and would replace Rutherford with SVM.
UAT offered seven new shares in its share capital for every nine shares in Pilot, and 33 pence for each Pilot warrant.
Pilot was established to invest in small UK-quoted companies, aiming to create value by providing management of companies in which it invests with support as they grow their businesses.
